title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation
layout_note: Two parallel training branches arranged 2 x 2. Top row: the input-image set (left) and the model being fine-tuned (right). Bottom row: the frozen model (left) and a second copy of the fine-tuned model (right). The two right-hand copies are joined by a vertical double-headed arrow labelled Shared Weights, and each branch's loss is a dashed elbow arc around the outer edge of the figure (Reconstruction Loss along the top, Class-Specific Prior Preservation Loss along the bottom).
grouping: No background panels. Groups are formed by rounded black-outlined frames: a large frame around three input photos with a bold caption below it (Input images (~3-5)), and narrow tall frames around stacks of three generated images beside each model glyph. Colour families mark model state: red = frozen model, yellow = model being fine-tuned.
shapes_depth: The diffusion model is abstracted as a flat bow-tie glyph (two triangles meeting at a waist) with 'Text -> Image' written across it in bold, with no network detail. Each glyph has a small grey noise square at its left and a quoted prompt in a handwriting-style font with a thick black arrow into it from above (top row) or below (bottom row). Loss arcs are dashed black elbow lines with arrowheads, labelled in italic serif. Images are real photographs of dogs.
proposed_highlight: The model being fine-tuned is drawn in yellow and the frozen reference model in red with a padlock icon. The paper's training objective is shown as its two named losses on dashed arcs that wrap the top and bottom of the figure, and the unique identifier appears only in the top prompt ('A [V] dog' versus 'A dog').
lesson: When the figure explains a training procedure rather than an architecture, the network can be one coloured bow-tie glyph labelled 'Text -> Image', with frozen versus trained shown by fill colour plus a padlock and each loss drawn as a dashed labelled arc between the image sets it compares.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2208.12242); venue CVPR as recorded in refs.json (venue_source semantic-scholar). The figure is a single raster image in the PDF (refs crop recorded one embedded image covering almost the whole crop), so kb measure cannot separate the photos: photo_share is null and the palette includes the dog photos and noise squares.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

arrangement.units: Two lanes stacked: the subject lane (input photos, fine-tuned model, outputs) above, the prior lane (frozen model, fine-tuned model, outputs) below; no frames, the lanes are separated by space.
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos in a framed group, quoted prompts with an arrow into each model
arrangement.losses_at: each lane's loss is a dashed labelled arc along that lane's outer edge — reconstruction loss along the top, prior-preservation loss along the bottom
arrangement.shared: the fine-tuned model is drawn once in each lane, the copies joined by a vertical 'Shared Weights' double arrow

core.what: two losses each pair a fine-tuned model's output frame with a target frame: a dashed arc over the top joins the '[V] dog' outputs to the input photos (reconstruction), a dashed arc under the bottom joins the 'A dog' outputs to the frozen model's outputs (prior preservation)

relations.form: each loss is a dashed elbow arc with an italic label running round the outside of the figure between the two image frames it compares, top arc for reconstruction, bottom arc for prior preservation
the two yellow fine-tuned bow-ties are stacked in the right column and joined by a vertical double arrow labelled 'Shared Weights'
the bottom row puts a red padlocked frozen bow-tie (left) and a yellow trainable copy (right) side by side on the same prompt 'A dog', each followed by its frame of three generated dogs
each prompt enters its bow-tie as a short vertical arrow (from above in the top row, from below in the bottom row) while a grey noise square sits at the bow-tie's left without an arrow

channels.colour: model state: yellow = being fine-tuned, red + padlock = frozen; all other elements are black and white or real photos
channels.shape: bow-tie = text-to-image model, rounded tall frame = a set of images, grey square = noise
channels.line: solid arrows = prompt input and the weight-sharing link; dashed arcs = losses
channels.frame: a rounded black frame = one image set (input photos or a model's outputs)

quality.strengths: Images are drawn as real photos (the actual chow-chow and generated dogs), and both losses are drawn between the image sets they compare rather than as boxes; frozen vs trained is a single clean colour channel reinforced by a padlock; the shared-weights link is a short straight vertical arrow between aligned copies.
quality.weaknesses: Neither the noise squares nor the model outputs are connected by arrows, so the reader infers that the noise enters and the frame is produced; the two loss arcs are long detours round the whole figure; the generated '[V] dog' frame is small compared with the input photo frame it is compared with.

insights.structure: A 2 x 2 arrangement: top row the input-photo frame and the yellow fine-tuned model, bottom row the red frozen model and a second yellow copy, with the two yellow copies joined by a vertical 'Shared Weights' double arrow.
insights.data: Each model is a flat bow-tie glyph with 'Text -> Image' across it, a small grey noise square at its left, a quoted prompt ('A [V] dog', 'A dog') in a handwriting font, and a tall frame of three real dog photos as output.
insights.emphasis: Fill colour marks model state (red with a padlock = frozen, yellow = being fine-tuned), and the two losses are dashed elbow arcs labelled in italic serif that run around the outside of the figure.
insights.flow: Prompts enter vertically (from above in the top row, from below in the bottom row); the reconstruction loss arc runs across the top from the generated images back to the input photos, the prior-preservation arc along the bottom between the two generated stacks.
insights.avoid: The noise squares float unconnected to the left of each model, and the frozen model's output stack is not labelled as the target of the prior loss.
